intro.title: Write a balanced parentheses checker
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that checks if a string of parentheses is balanced. A balanced string means every opening parenthesis '(' has a corresponding closing parenthesis ')' in the correct order. You will learn to use a stack data structure to track parentheses as you iterate through the string. This exercise will help you practice fundamental JavaScript concepts like loops, conditionals, and array methods. By the end, you'll have a working checker that returns true for balanced strings and false for unbalanced ones.
intro.usecase: Balanced parentheses checking is essential in code editors and IDEs like VS Code, which validate syntax in real-time by ensuring every opening bracket has a matching closing one. This pattern also powers form validation in web applications, such as checking mathematical expressions in calculator inputs or JSON/XML structures in configuration panels. Developers implement these checkers to prevent runtime errors in templating engines, build tools that parse configuration files, and even in UI component libraries that dynamically render nested components.
